notes: Fixture diffs are synthetic but reference real repo paths so CODEOWNERS resolution is genuine. Ownership facts asserted here were verified against .github/CODEOWNERS and src/Sql/dbo layout at commit 6798eb683.

evals.name: ranks-cross-team-write-above-read
evals.prompt: I reworked the attachment storage validation in CipherService before putting it up as a PR. The diff is at .claude/skills/reviewing-data-boundaries/evals/fixtures/01-vault-writes-organization.diff. Can you review it? I mainly want to know if I've created any coupling problems for the team.
evals.expected_output: Reports three cross-boundary writes as the most severe findings: Organization.Storage, Organization.RevisionDate, and the full-row ReplaceAsync persistence call. Reports the Organization.MaxCollections read as a lower-severity contract candidate, and recommends a command or event rather than a read interface.
assertions: Identifies Organization.Storage as a cross-boundary WRITE, not merely a read
Also identifies the Organization.RevisionDate assignment as a cross-boundary write
Identifies _organizationRepository.ReplaceAsync(org) as a full-row write covering every mapped Organization column, not just the two assigned
Ranks the write(s) as more severe than the read, and presents them first
Identifies the Organization.MaxCollections access as a cross-boundary read
Names the code owner as team-vault-dev (Vault) and the data owner as admin-console
Recommends a command or an event for the write, and states that a read interface cannot fix a write
Does NOT report the unchanged org.MaxStorageGb.HasValue context line as a new finding

evals.name: no-false-positive-on-same-team-change
evals.prompt: Quick review before I push please. Diff is at .claude/skills/reviewing-data-boundaries/evals/fixtures/02-clean-same-team.diff, it is just the cipher restore path in CipherService.
evals.expected_output: Reports no cross-team data boundary crossings. Explains that Cipher is Vault-owned so Vault code touching it is not a crossing, and that nameof(Organization.Seats) is a compile-time string rather than a data access.
assertions: Reports ZERO cross-boundary crossings / no violations
States that Cipher is Vault-owned, so Vault code writing it is same-team and not a crossing
Explicitly states that nameof(Organization.Seats) is not a data access and does not count
Does not invent a finding about Organization

evals.name: catches-helper-hidden-and-pattern-reads
evals.prompt: I added a storage guard to the Send file upload path. The diff is at .claude/skills/reviewing-data-boundaries/evals/fixtures/03-tools-hidden-helper-read.diff. Does this look OK from a data ownership standpoint?
evals.expected_output: Flags the StorageBytesRemaining() call as a hidden read of Organization.Storage and Organization.MaxStorageGb, flags the property-pattern read of UseTotp, identifies Tools as the code owner and admin-console as the data owner, and classifies both as reads (contract candidates) rather than writes.
assertions: Flags organization.StorageBytesRemaining() as an indirect/hidden column read
Names BOTH Storage and MaxStorageGb as the columns that helper reads
Flags the property-pattern access organization is { UseTotp: true } as a read of UseTotp
Names the code owner as team-tools-dev (Tools) and the data owner as admin-console
